scenes.name: an answer, one token every thirty milliseconds
scenes.visual: Dark canvas, one continuous shot, no camera move. Scene options: default fade-in, fadeOut:false (handoff below). Chat window: a rounded panel x 300-1,620, y 130-760, thin blue outline (blue = structure). Inside, top right: a grey user bubble ending at x 1,500, y 195, text 'Why is the sky blue?' (34 px), with a user icon at (1,560, 195). Below, a sparkle icon for the assistant at (360, 270). The answer streams in from x 400, y 270, 32 px white text, line height 46 px, wrapping before x 1,560 (about seven lines). Each token lands as a faint blue pill and relaxes into plain text 0.3 s later. The answer, exactly: 'Sunlight looks white, but it is really a mix of every colour of the rainbow. On its way down through the air, it keeps bumping into tiny gas molecules, mostly nitrogen and oxygen. Each bump can knock a little of the light off course and send it sideways. This is called scattering, and it does not treat all colours equally. Short wavelengths, the blues, scatter far more strongly than long ones, the reds. So blue light reaches your eyes from every direction, and the whole sky glows blue.' The freeze point is just after ' blues'. Before it: 74 tokens. Held back for the slow-motion section: the 29 after it. Bottom band: a tick track, a thin grey line x 160-1,640 at y 880, with a stopwatch icon (80 px) at (1,720, 880) and a mono readout (30 px) at (1,720, 960): the time since the last token in whole milliseconds, '0 ms' to '30 ms'. Track mapping: the track is chart paper scrolling left. Each landed token drops a white tick, 24 px tall, at x 1,640, next to the stopwatch. Ticks sit 60 px apart and fade as they reach x 160. Only the arrival rate changes, never the spacing. When paused the paper stops, with about 25 crisp ticks in view. In 20x slow motion it moves 100 px/s, a smooth 3.3 px per frame, one crisp tick every 0.6 s. True speed (one tick per 30 ms, 2,000 px/s) must be drawn differently, because render.py seeks frame by frame at 30 fps with no motion blur. The paper would move 66.7 px per frame, just past the 60 px spacing, so crisp ticks would seem to crawl slowly left at about 200 px/s. They would be countable, only twice the slow-motion speed, and the true-speed vs slow-motion contrast would be lost. So at true speed draw no crisp ticks. Draw each tick as a horizontal streak 66 px long and 24 px tall: white at its left end, fading to nothing at its right, the trail it left during one frame. Neighbouring streaks overlap into one shimmering grey band. Shift the whole streak pattern each frame by a seeded random offset of 0-60 px (S.rand keyed to the frame number, floor(t × 30)), so it never settles into a steady crawl. The readout likewise shows a seeded random whole number from 0 to 29 ms on every frame: a flicker, not a count. (Sampled every 33.3 ms, a real 30 ms sawtooth would step only 3.3 ms per frame and read as a slow count.) A grey speed tag (26 px) centred above the stopwatch at (1,720, 800) reads 'paused' or 'slowed 20×' whenever the stream is not at true speed, and is absent at true speed. Handoff: on 'That number' (b3), the chat window, answer text, track, ticks, bracket, stopwatch, readout and speed tag all dim to 20% over 0.5 s, so the stamp that grows over the answer is never white on white. In the scene's last second (the 1 s tail after the voice, from 15.57 s), they fade out fully over 0.8 s. Only the white stamp is left: '≈ 30 ms' (96 px, centred at 960, 500) with 'per token' (40 px, grey, centred at 960, 580). s02 opens on exactly that frame. The idea: an answer is a fast, even drumbeat of small pieces, about 30 ms apart.

beats.say: Ask a chatbot a question, and the answer streams out, one small piece at a time.
beats.show: On 'Ask a chatbot', the chat window draws on and 'Why is the sky blue?' types into the user bubble. On 'the answer', the sparkle icon pulses. The stream is keyed to text position, not to a spoken word. It runs at true speed, 33 tokens a second, starting at b2 minus 74 × 30 ms (b2 - 2.22 s). In the measured audio that falls just after 'streams out', and the freeze point arrives exactly as b2 begins. If the pill list built differs from 74 tokens, use start = b2 - N × 0.03 s. Tokens flash as blue pills and settle into text. The track runs as the true-speed streak band set out in the scene visual: a shimmering grey blur, too fast to count, while the stopwatch readout flickers through random values.

beats.say: Each piece is a token, a word or part of one. They arrive on a steady beat, about one every thirty milliseconds.
beats.show: On 'Each piece', the stream and the paper freeze just after ' blues'. The streak band snaps to crisp ticks exactly 60 px apart, about 25 in view and countable for the first time. The readout stops at '0 ms', since ' blues' has just landed, and the speed tag fades in: 'paused'. The newest six tokens stand apart as blue pills with thin gaps: ' Short', ' wave', 'lengths', ',', ' the', ' blues'. The rest of the answer dims to 50%. On 'part of one', ' wave' and 'lengths' glow together. A small bracket draws under them on the empty line below, labelled 'one word, two tokens', with a grey tag 'illustrative split' beside it. On 'steady beat', the bracket and its labels fade, the pills relax into text and the answer undims. The stream resumes in 20x slow motion with the held-back text (', scatter far more strongly than long ones, the reds…'): one token every 0.6 s, each dropping a crisp tick 60 px from the last, the paper gliding a smooth 3.3 px per frame. The tag swaps to 'slowed 20×'. The stopwatch readout now visibly counts 0 → 30 ms between ticks and resets on each one. On 'thirty milliseconds', a bracket draws between the two newest ticks, labelled '≈ 30 ms' above it, and rides left with them at 100 px/s.

beats.say: That number is what this film is about.
beats.show: The slow beat continues: about nine held-back tokens land in all (5.5 s from 'steady' to the closing fade), so the answer never finishes, and it does not need to. On 'That number', everything else dims to 20% over 0.5 s: the chat window, answer text, track, ticks, bracket, stopwatch, readout and speed tag. The dimmed stream keeps landing tokens and dropping ticks underneath. At the same time the '≈ 30 ms' label lifts off its bracket, grows, and glides to the centre (960, 500) as the white 96 px stamp '≈ 30 ms'. It passes over answer lines 5 and 6 (y 454 and 500), which are now at 20%, so the stamp reads cleanly. 'per token' fades in beneath it at (960, 580). In the scene's last second the dimmed elements fade out fully, as set in the scene handoff, and only the stamp remains.

scenes.name: a sliver of arithmetic
scenes.visual: Opens on the stamp exactly as s01 left it. Scene options: fadeIn:false, fadeOut:false. One continuous shot, no camera move. A single horizontal bar across the centre, x 210-1,710, y 640-720: 1,500 px stands for the 30 ms of one token, 50 px per millisecond, drawn to scale. It is a proportion bar, the token's total time gathered by kind. It is not a clock running left to right, so it has no time ticks and nothing labelled 'start'. A dimension line under it (y 750, x 210-1,710) carries the label '≈ 30 ms per token' (40 px, centred at 960, 790), which is the stamp itself, keeping its '≈'. A blue pill 'one token' sits above the right end, centred at (1,710, 590): the thing those 30 ms produce. An amber-outlined chip icon (96 px) sits at (300, 380). The bar fills in stages. b1: outline only. b2: an amber 5 px sliver at x 210-215. b3 onward: the other 1,495 px filled flat grey, the white label 'something else: over 99%' inside it, and a large soft '?' above it. A magnifier inset (x 460-1,460, y 250-420) is open only from 'all of it' in b2 to the start of b3. Colour: amber = arithmetic, grey = the unexplained rest, blue = token and model. The idea: the arithmetic for one token is enormous as a count, yet gathered together it fills a 5 px sliver of a 1,500 px bar.

beats.say: Making one token takes a staggering amount of arithmetic, about a hundred billion multiplications and additions.
beats.show: On 'Making', the stamp shrinks and drops to (960, 790) as the label '≈ 30 ms per token'. At the same time the bar outline draws outward from the centre to full width, and the dimension line draws beneath it. The 'one token' pill pops in above the right end. On 'arithmetic', the chip icon appears, and an amber counter appears to its right (left edge x 380, y 380, 64 px mono) with a flickering '× +' glyph. On 'a hundred billion', the counter runs from 0 to '≈ 100,000,000,000'. A grey label settles under it, left-anchored at (380, 450): 'multiplications and additions'.

beats.say: Yet a modern data-centre chip could get through all of it in about a tenth of a millisecond.
beats.show: On 'data-centre chip', the chip icon brightens. On 'get through', the counter's digits and label collapse into a small amber block, which drops into the bar's left end and settles as an amber sliver exactly 5 px wide, all within 0.6 s. On 'all of it', a magnifier opens above it. Two thin grey guide lines draw from the bar's first millisecond (x 210 and x 260, at y 640) up to the bottom corners of an inset panel (x 460-1,460, y 250-420, thin white outline), which opens over 0.5 s. Inside the panel, a grey tag '×20' sits at the top right. In the inset, 1 ms spans the full 1,000 px, so the sliver is a clear 100 px amber block at the left (y 275-335). A dimension line near the inset's bottom spans its full width, with '1 ms' in a gap at its centre. On 'a tenth of a millisecond', an amber tag lands right of the block: 'arithmetic ≈ 0.1 ms'. Measured audio: 'all' at 11.05 s and b3 at 14.07 s, so the open inset is fully readable for about 2.5 s, and its amber tag for about 1.8 s.

beats.say: Back at true scale, the arithmetic is just this sliver, under one percent of the thirty milliseconds. More than ninety-nine percent is something else.
beats.show: On 'Back at true scale', the inset collapses back down its guide lines into the bar's first millisecond over 0.6 s, finishing on 'scale', and the lines retract. The 5 px sliver is left at true scale. On 'this sliver', a short amber pointer drops onto the sliver's top from a tag left-anchored at (240, 580): 'all the arithmetic'. On 'under one percent', the tag swaps to 'arithmetic: under 1%'. On 'thirty milliseconds', the dimension line and its label '≈ 30 ms per token' glow once, so the share is heard and seen against the whole bar. On 'ninety-nine percent', the remaining 1,495 px fill with flat grey in one soft fade, not a left-to-right sweep, so the bar does not read as a clock. On 'something else', the white label 'something else: over 99%' lands inside the grey at (960, 680). A large soft grey '?' (96 px) fades up above the grey at (1,240, 560).

beats.say: The chip isn't slow, and the model behind the chatbot isn't badly written. In one token's time, the chip could do the arithmetic for about three hundred tokens. So what fills the rest?
beats.show: On 'isn't slow', the chip icon pulses amber. On 'the model behind the chatbot', a blue model-file icon (80 px) appears just below the chip at (300, 480), with the label 'model' to its right, and glows once. On 'In one token's time', copies of the 5 px amber sliver start stamping into the bar from left to right over the grey, accelerating. Layering: the copies sit on top of the grey strip. The 'arithmetic: under 1%' tag and its pointer sit above the bar and stay as they are. The white inside label 'something else: over 99%' fades to 0 over 0.3 s as the tiling front reaches its left edge, so no white text sits on amber. An amber counter at (960, 470) runs from 1 to 300 under a grey label at (960, 410): 'tokens of arithmetic'. Time it so the last copy lands, tiling the bar exactly to its right end, as 'three hundred' is spoken (31.50 s in the measured audio, 3.7 s after 'In' at 27.78 s); the counter settles on '≈ 300'. On 'So what fills the rest?', the 299 copies and the counter fade out over 0.6 s, the grey shows through again with its inside label fading back up with it, and the '?' pulses once on 'rest'. Handoff: in the scene's last second the chip icon, model icon and counter label fade. The final frame holds exactly: the bar at y 640-720 (sliver x 210-215, grey x 215-1,710) with 'something else: over 99%' inside; the 'arithmetic: under 1%' tag and its pointer; the '?' at (1,240, 560); the 'one token' pill at (1,710, 590); and the dimension line with '≈ 30 ms per token' at (960, 790).

scenes.name: two numbers, and a wall
scenes.visual: Opens on s02's final frame exactly. Scene options: fadeIn:false, default fade-out, the film's first fade to black. One continuous shot, no camera move. In b1-b2 the bar group eases down 160 px (bar y 800-880). Its tag, pointer, '?', dimension line and '≈ 30 ms per token' label move with it; the label goes to y 950. As it moves, the 'one token' pill and the label inside the grey fade out, and the 'arithmetic: under 1%' tag and pointer dim to 30%, so at most five text items besides numbers are at full strength while the facts arrive. That frees the upper area for three facts. On the left, a stopwatch readout and a model file; on the right, a chip specification sheet. Positions: stopwatch icon (110 px) at (260, 330). Readout '≈ 30 ms' (72 px mono, white) left-anchored at x 340, y 330, about 300 px wide so it ends near x 642, with 'per token' (30 px grey) at (340, 405). Model-file icon (96 px, blue) at (260, 540), with the label 'model size' (36 px) left-anchored at x 340, y 540. Spec-sheet card x 1,000-1,640, y 180-620: header 'chip spec sheet' (36 px) at its top left, and six grey placeholder lines at y 300, 350, 400, 450, 500, 550, from x 1,040 to 1,600. In b3-b4 everything except the bar's two parts clears, and the grey 99% restacks into a wall. Wall geometry: floor line y 880, wall x 1,300-1,520, y 320-880. Title left-aligned at x 160, y 330, 110 px display type; about 950 px wide, so it ends near x 1,110, clear of the wall. Colour: amber for the calculation line and the sliver, coral for the memory line and the wall, blue for the model and the token, white and grey for text. The idea: a promise that the 30 ms can be worked out from the model's size and two chip numbers. Then the 99% becomes a wall a token cannot pass, and it gets its name.

beats.say: By the end, you'll work out the thirty milliseconds yourself, from the model's size and two numbers on a chip's specification sheet.
beats.show: On 'By the end', the bar group eases down 160 px, carrying its dimension line and label. At the same moment the 'one token' pill and the inside label 'something else: over 99%' fade out over 0.4 s, and the 'arithmetic: under 1%' tag and pointer dim to 30%. The sliver, the grey strip and the '?' stay at full strength. On 'thirty milliseconds', the label '≈ 30 ms per token' lifts out and flies up-left, and the dimension line fades. The label becomes the readout '≈ 30 ms' / 'per token' as the stopwatch icon pops in beside it. On 'yourself', a small pencil icon draws a white underline beneath '≈ 30 ms'. On 'model's size', the blue model-file icon and its 'model size' label slide in below the stopwatch. On 'two numbers', the spec-sheet card slides in from the right with its header and six grey placeholder lines. On 'specification sheet', two of the lines (y 350 and y 450) brighten.

beats.say: How fast it calculates, and how fast its memory delivers the model. For any model, on any chip.
beats.show: On 'calculates', the line at y 350 resolves into amber text 'operations per second: ?', and it glows once together with the amber sliver on the bar below. On 'memory', the line at y 450 resolves into coral text 'bytes per second: ?'. A thin coral thread draws from that line's left end (1,030, 450) to just right of the '≈ 30 ms' readout (660, 330). On 'the model', a short blue thread draws straight up from the model-file icon to the stopwatch (x 260, y 492 to 388), and '≈ 30 ms' flashes coral once. The amber line gets no thread to the stopwatch. The values stay '?' on purpose. On 'any model, on any chip', a fan of three faint chip icons and three model-file icons of different sizes riffles behind the card and settles.

beats.say: And the ninety-nine percent has a name.
beats.show: On 'And', these fade out over 0.4 s: the stopwatch, readout and underline, the model icon and its label, both threads, the spec-sheet card and fan, and the dimmed 'arithmetic: under 1%' tag and pointer. A thin grey floor line draws from x 160 to 1,760 along the bar's bottom edge (y 880). On 'ninety-nine percent', the grey strip breaks into 28 equal pieces, about 53 × 80 px each. They fly right and stack, staggered over 1.0 s and finished by 'has', into a wall at x 1,300-1,520, y 320-880: 14 courses of two 110 × 40 px bricks, about the same area as the strip. The bricks warm from grey to coral as they rise. The '?' rides up on the top course to (1,410, 270). The amber sliver stays on the floor at x 210-215, tiny. On 'has a name', an unlabelled blue token pill (60 × 40) glides in from the left edge along the floor (y 860) and passes the sliver. It stops dead against the wall's left face at x 1,300 with a small 8 px recoil, just before b4 begins.

On 'The', the '?' fades, and the title writes on in large white display type, left-aligned at x 160, y 330, by one rule: the three words start 0.15 s apart from 'The' (at b4, b4 + 0.15 s and b4 + 0.30 s) and each writes on in 0.3 s, so 'The Memory Wall' is complete 0.6 s after b4 begins, before 'wall' is spoken. On 'wall', the bricks pulse coral once. There is no subtitle: it would get under a second, too short to read seven words. The voice sets the scene's length. Measured audio: b4 begins at 17.36 s, 'wall' at 18.04 s, the voice ends at 18.35 s, and the scene ends at 19.37 s, 2.0 s after b4 begins. The engine's fade to black starts at 18.87 s. So the complete title holds at full strength for about 0.9 s (17.96 to 18.87 s), then fades with the scene over 0.5 s. Do not plan a longer hold; the pipeline has no per-scene tail.

checks.claim: The 30 ms is the H200 division from the film bible: 140 GB / 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms, rounded to 'about thirty milliseconds'. It is derived later, in ch02, and only teased here.
One token every 30 ms is about 33 tokens a second, the true streaming speed in s01 b1

Storyboard s01: by word-and-punctuation count, with 'wavelengths' split into two pills, the answer is 103 tokens. 74 come before the freeze point after ' blues' and 29 are held back. At 30 ms each, the 74 stream in 2.22 s, so the stream starts 2.22 s before b2. (This replaces the earlier wrong check: '100 tokens in two sentences, 3 s'.)
checks.python: import re; f=lambda s: len(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z']+|[.,]", s))+s.count('wavelengths'); a='Sunlight looks white, but it is really a mix of every colour of the rainbow. On its way down through the air, it keeps bumping into tiny gas molecules, mostly nitrogen and oxygen. Each bump can knock a little of the light off course and send it sideways. This is called scattering, and it does not treat all colours equally. Short wavelengths, the blues'; b=', scatter far more strongly than long ones, the reds. So blue light reaches your eyes from every direction, and the whole sky glows blue.'; print(f(a), f(b), f(a)+f(b), round(f(a)*0.03, 2))

checks.claim: Storyboard s01: 20x slow motion makes the 30 ms gap 0.6 s of screen time

Storyboard s01 chart paper: ticks 60 px apart. At true speed that is 60 px per 30 ms = 2,000 px/s; at 20x slow motion, 60 px per 0.6 s = 100 px/s. The 1,480 px track holds about 25 ticks, and a tick crosses it in 0.74 s at true speed.

Storyboard s01 (measured Kokoro audio): slow motion runs from 'steady' at 10.10 s to the closing fade at 15.57 s, which is the 16.57 s scene minus its 1 s tail. That is 5.5 s, about 9 tokens at 0.6 s each, well within the 29 held back. The true-speed stream starts at 5.93 - 2.22 = 3.71 s, just after 'streams' (3.14 s) and 'out' (3.58 s).
'About a hundred billion multiplications and additions' is the round power of ten for 70e9 weights x 2 = 140 billion operations (log10 = 11.15, so about 10^11); ch05 explains the rounding
About 10^11 operations at about 10^15 operations per second = 10^-4 s = 0.1 ms, 'about a tenth of a millisecond' (a peak-rate capability, hence 'could get through')
Arithmetic share of the 30 ms: 0.1 / 30 = 0.33%, 'under one percent'

Everything else: 100 - 0.33 = 99.67%. Spoken as 'more than ninety-nine percent' and shown as 'something else: over 99%', so voice and screen agree; s03 b3's 'the ninety-nine percent has a name' names that same share, as fig 67 does

Robustness of 'over 99%' with unrounded numbers. The H200 has the same 989e12 ops/s dense 16-bit compute as the H100, with 4.8 TB/s. That gives 140e9 ops in 0.1416 ms against a 29.17 ms token: 0.49% arithmetic, 99.51% other. Both the rounded and the unrounded versions clear 99%.
'About three hundred tokens' of arithmetic in one token's time: 30 / 0.1 = 300 with round numbers
Round-number figure, as in ch05: with unrounded H200 numbers the ratio is 29.17 / 0.1416 = 206, about 200, so the narration hedges with 'about'
Storyboard s02 scale: 1,500 px = 30 ms gives 50 px per ms; the 0.1 ms sliver is 5 px; the remainder is 1,495 px
Storyboard s02 b4: 300 copies of the 5 px sliver tile the 1,500 px bar exactly
Storyboard s02 b2 magnifier: the inset shows 1 ms over 1,000 px, 20x the bar's 50 px per ms, so the 0.1 ms sliver is 100 px. This replaces the tenfold camera zoom.

Storyboard s03 wall: 14 courses of two 110 x 40 px bricks = 28 bricks, 220 px thick and 560 px tall (y 320-880). Its area is 123,200 px2, about the grey strip's 1,495 x 80 = 119,600 px2 (3% more), so the restacking does not exaggerate. Each strip piece is about 53 x 80 px.

Storyboard s01 true speed vs the 30 fps render: the paper moves 66.7 px per frame against 60 px tick spacing, so crisp ticks would alias to a 6.7 px per frame (200 px/s) crawl, only 2x the slow-motion 100 px/s; slow motion is a smooth 3.3 px per frame. The readout, sampled every 33.3 ms, would step 3.3 ms per frame through a 30 ms sawtooth. Hence the 66 px streaks, seeded random offsets and a random readout at true speed.

Storyboard s02 b2-b3 (re-measured Kokoro audio after the edit): the inset opens on 'all' (11.05 s) over 0.5 s and collapses on 'Back' (b3, 14.069 s), so it is fully readable about 2.5 s; its 'arithmetic ≈ 0.1 ms' tag, landing on 'tenth' (12.308 s), about 1.8 s; the 0.6 s collapse ends at 14.67 s, on 'scale' (14.82 s)
Storyboard s02 b4 (re-measured audio): the 300 copies stamp from 'In' (27.779 s) to 'three' (31.496 s), 3.7 s

Storyboard s03 b4 (re-measured audio): scene 19.367 s, b4 at 17.362 s. The engine fade starts at 18.867 s; with a 0.15 s stagger and 0.3 s write-on the title is complete at 17.962 s and holds 0.905 s at full strength; the scene ends 2.0 s after b4 begins

Storyboard s03: the readout '≈ 30 ms' is 7 monospace characters at 72 px (0.6 em advance), about 302 px wide, so left-anchored at x 340 it ends near x 642, and the coral thread ends at x 660, clear of it
Chapter length after the edit (re-measured audio): 16.57 + 35.23 + 19.37 = 71.2 s, inside the 60-100 s target
